bugClass.title: Provider turns bypass declared local verification
bugClass.cause: A managed module-task flow declares a local verification operation, but after a provider result it transitions to review or completion without executing that operation or requiring evidence that it ran. This leaves the decision dependent on provider output rather than the declared local check.
bugClass.criteria: Classify when both conditions hold: (1) the module-task flow has a declared local verification operation, such as a command or check; and (2) a provider-result-to-review or completion path neither executes that operation nor requires proof of its execution. Either a missing execution step or a missing evidence gate is sufficient. Exclude code that only transports provider events, orchestration with no declared local command, Docker fixtures, and paths with an actual execution or evidence gate.

Lines 9–17 describe acceptance evidence requiring a checkpoint and verification record, but the excerpt does not establish that this evidence is used on the provider-result-to-review path or that a declared local command is skipped.

Lines 40–47 pass `config.moduleVerification` into `withModuleCandidate` and `reviewModule` for each completion check; this excerpt shows the declared module verification is part of the evaluation path, so it does not establish a bypass.
Lines 42–51 are explicitly the orchestrator-scope completion flow (`scope: 'orchestrator'`) and evaluate configured orchestration checks; the class concerns a managed module-task flow.

At `moduleCompletionMeasurement.ts:11-23`, missing runnable verification files or a configured `moduleVerification` command raises `CompletionCheckError`, and the code proceeds to construct and run a local verification command. This is a guard and local check, not a provider bypass.

Lines 14–26 show a real guard: when `task.check` is configured, `taskCheckLoop` runs `runTaskCheck` and continues after failures. This is the declared-check execution path, not a provider-result bypass.

Lines 34–36 show accepted reviews call `acceptanceEvidence(root, before, review.evidence!)` before proceeding, a visible evidence gate at this review site. The excerpt does not establish a provider-result-to-review bypass.
